newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares seen range-bound, seeking new impetus.
newsitem.headline: German shares seen range-bound, seeking new impetus.

text.p: German shares, fractionally higher in late Thursday trade, were seen budging little over the coming trading days until U.S. monetary authorities meet to consider U.S. interest rates next week.

Germany's IBIS index of all-day electronic trade traded 4.21 points up at 2,625.41 amid limited volumes and was not expected to be affected much by the expiry of future and options contracts on the DAX this week.
"The DAX itself looks to be in a very tight range until the FOMC meets next week (September 24)," one dealer said. September DAX futures meanwhile traded five points up at 2,627.
Dollar trading against the mark, currently hovering around 1.5110, was also seen on hold until the FOMC meeting.
With shares in individual stocks light, traders said various market rumours had been circulating.

Shares in Bayerische Vereinsbank rose nine pfennigs higher at 53.61 on a resurgence of market talk, quickly dismissed by most, that the banking sector was readying itself for a series of consolidation within which Vereinsbank would be a takeover candidate.
